Released: 28 August 2026

Version 2.2.0 adds the `pgd` installation scenario, collects the container registry settings of a `HybridControlPlane` under a single `spec.registry` block, changes what the operator installs when `spec.scenarios` is omitted, and reports the resources that blocked a failed component deploy in the resource status.

## Highlights

- **`spec.scenarios` accepts a new `pgd` value, and operator 2.2.0 is the earliest version that does.** An HM version that moves Postgres Distributed components into a `pgd` scenario can't run on an earlier operator. Nothing adds `pgd` for you.

- **A `HybridControlPlane` that omits `spec.scenarios` now installs only the `core` scenario.** Earlier operator versions filled in a default set. List the scenarios you need explicitly before you upgrade.

- **Registry configuration moves to `spec.registry`, and the fields it replaces are deprecated.** `spec.imageRegistry`, `spec.imagePullSecrets`, and the registry settings under `spec.kappController` and `spec.beaconAgent.provisioning` are still honored, but they now produce a deprecation warning and will be removed in a future API version.

- **A control plane waiting for an `HMRegistry` no longer stays stale until the operator restarts.** Repairing a registry that was rejected for a reason that left its URIs unchanged did not wake the control plane, so an installation or upgrade stayed pending.

## Features

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary><code>pgd</code> installation scenario
</summary><hr/><p><strong>Action required.</strong> <code>spec.scenarios</code> accepts a new <code>pgd</code> value, covering the operator that manages Postgres Distributed clusters. Nothing adds <code>pgd</code> for you, and no other scenario pulls it in. An installation that uses those clusters and upgrades to an HM version whose collections have moved them out of <code>core</code> must add <code>pgd</code> — once the operator is on 2.2.0 or later, and before bumping <code>spec.version</code> — or the components are removed along with the data the clusters hold. Operator versions before 2.2.0 don't recognize the value, so add it only after upgrading the operator and read the resource back to confirm it persisted.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Unified registry configuration under <code>spec.registry</code>
</summary><hr/><p><code>spec.registry</code> gathers the container registry settings that were previously spread across the <code>HybridControlPlane</code> spec: <code>spec.registry.url</code> and <code>spec.registry.imagePullSecrets</code> for pulling images, <code>spec.registry.tls.caCerts</code> and <code>spec.registry.tls.dangerousSkipTLSVerify</code> for the trust used to reach it, and <code>spec.registry.discovery.enabled</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>provider</code>, <code>authenticationType</code>, and <code>credentialsSecretName</code> for image set discovery. A value under <code>spec.registry</code> takes precedence over its older counterpart, and where <code>spec.registry</code> is unset the older field still applies, so existing manifests keep working unchanged. When you point at an in-cluster registry with <code>spec.hmRegistryRef</code>, the operator populates these fields for you.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Failed resources are reported in <code>HybridControlPlane</code> status
</summary><hr/><p>When a component fails to deploy, <code>status.components[].failedResources</code> names the resources that blocked it — kind, API version, name, namespace, and the error — each with the recent warning events that explain why, including events raised against the pods, replica sets, and volume claims those resources own. Read it with <code>kubectl describe hybridcontrolplane</code> to see why a deploy is stuck instead of hunting through component namespaces. The list holds at most 10 resources, with at most 5 events each, and is cleared once the component deploys.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Enhancements

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Per-component operator logs and optional JSON log output
</summary><hr/><p>Every operator log record now carries the component being reconciled, and the operator renders its logs as human-readable text with that component as a per-line prefix, so the output of a single component — including the output of <code>kapp</code> itself — can be followed in <code>kubectl logs</code>. To send logs to a collector that parses them, set <code>controllerManager.manager.logFormat</code> to <code>json</code> in the operator Helm chart, which passes <code>--log-json</code> to the manager and emits one JSON record per line instead.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Security Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Updated Helm libraries in the operator image
</summary><hr/><p>The operator is built against newer Helm libraries, which clears the vulnerabilities reported against the versions it shipped with in 2.1.0. No configuration change is needed.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Changes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Only the <code>core</code> scenario is added when <code>spec.scenarios</code> is omitted
</summary><hr/><p><strong>Action required.</strong> A <code>HybridControlPlane</code> that leaves <code>spec.scenarios</code> unset now installs the <code>core</code> scenario alone. Earlier operator versions filled in a default set covering <code>core</code>, <code>dbaas</code>, <code>ai</code>, <code>analytics</code>, <code>migration</code>, and <code>marketplace</code>. List every scenario you want explicitly, and check an existing manifest that relies on the old default before you apply it against operator 2.2 or later: re-applying it removes the components belonging to the scenarios that are no longer listed, along with the data they hold. <code>core</code> is still added for you when your list leaves it out, and scenario dependencies are still resolved automatically.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Bug Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>A control plane waiting for an <code>HMRegistry</code> could stay stale until the operator restarted
</summary><hr/><p>The operator re-reconciled a <code>HybridControlPlane</code> only when the URIs of the <code>HMRegistry</code> it references changed. Repairing a registry that had been rejected for some other reason — an invalid volume size, for example — left the URIs untouched, so the control plane was never woken and its installation or upgrade stayed pending until the operator was restarted. The control plane is now retried every 30 seconds while it waits, and <code>status.message</code> names the registry it is waiting for until the registry is ready.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Postflight checks logged endless watch failures after a component was withdrawn
</summary><hr/><p>Postflight checks now read through the API server directly rather than through the operator's cache. Checking a component whose custom resource definition the running HM version no longer installs used to start a cache watch that retried for the lifetime of the operator, filling the log with list failures for a type that no longer exists.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>AWS load balancer annotations are no longer forced on EKS installations that disable load balancers
</summary><hr/><p>On EKS the operator defaults five AWS load balancer annotations on the <code>istio-ingressgateway</code> service: <code>aws-load-balancer-type</code>, <code>aws-load-balancer-scheme</code>, <code>aws-load-balancer-nlb-target-type</code>, <code>aws-load-balancer-target-group-attributes</code>, and <code>load-balancer-source-ranges</code>. It no longer adds them when <code>spec.globalParameters.load_balancer_mode</code> is <code>disabled</code> — the mode a NodePort-based installation uses — where earlier versions added them to every EKS installation and left one that provisions no load balancer carrying annotations that do not apply to it. Under every other mode the defaults still apply, and a value you set yourself in <code>spec.resourceAnnotations</code> is kept as it was.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Deprecations

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>The registry fields that <code>spec.registry</code> replaces are deprecated
</summary><hr/><p>Applying a <code>HybridControlPlane</code> that sets <code>spec.imageRegistry</code>, <code>spec.imagePullSecrets</code>, <code>spec.kappController.caCerts</code>, <code>spec.kappController.dangerousSkipTLSVerify</code>, the <code>spec.beaconAgent.provisioning</code> image discovery fields, or the <code>imageset_discovery_ca_certs</code> and <code>image_discovery_credentials_secret_name</code> parameters of the <code>upm-beacon</code> component returns an admission warning naming the <code>spec.registry</code> field to use instead. The values are still honored and nothing stops working, but move them to <code>spec.registry</code>, because they will be removed in a future API version. A warning is raised only where the deprecated field is the one taking effect, so a control plane whose registry settings come from an <code>HMRegistry</code> stays quiet.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
